review_notes: I read the whole file. I searched Mathlib for an existing quotient grading, quotient Decomposition or GradedRing instances, and found none, so the main construction is not a duplicate. The one clear overlap is the private `sourceComponent` helper, together with the identical structure literal inlined in `gradedComponent`. Both rebuild `AddSubgroup.ofClass (𝒜 i)`, which Mathlib already provides. The two structures are the same given `AddSubgroupClass σ A`. I did not check whether `AddSubgroup.ofClass` unifies with the inlined body under the `@[expose]` and `rfl` constraints described in the module docstring, so the replacement is untested. The finding is small in scope. Other items, such as the duplicated vanishing proof in `gradedDecompose`, are proof structure rather than competing concepts, so I excluded them.

findings.declaration: sourceComponent (and the inlined carrier in gradedComponent)
findings.excerpt:
private def sourceComponent (i : ι) : AddSubgroup A where
  carrier := 𝒜 i
  zero_mem' := zero_mem (𝒜 i)
  add_mem' := add_mem
  neg_mem' := neg_mem
findings.problem: The file builds the `AddSubgroup A` underlying a `SetLike`/`AddSubgroupClass` member by hand. It does so twice: once in the private `sourceComponent`, and once as an anonymous structure literal inside `gradedComponent`. Mathlib already has `AddSubgroup.ofClass`, the `to_additive` form of `Subgroup.ofClass`. Its docstring reads "The actual `AddSubgroup` obtained from an element of a `AddSubgroupClass`". Its hypotheses are exactly the file's `[SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A]` on an additive group. So `sourceComponent 𝒜 i` is `AddSubgroup.ofClass (𝒜 i)`, a competing local copy of an existing concept. It also forces the extra private `rfl` bridge lemma `gradedComponent_eq_privateConstruction`.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `sourceComponent`. Define `gradedComponent 𝒜 I i := AddSubgroup.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I).toAddMonoidHom (AddSubgroup.ofClass (𝒜 i))`. Then drop `gradedComponent_eq_privateConstruction`, or restate it against `AddSubgroup.ofClass`. Membership then goes through the existing `@[simps]` lemmas for `ofClass`. If the intent is to keep the body inlined for the exposed definition, inline `AddSubgroup.ofClass (𝒜 i)` instead of a hand-written structure literal.
findings.benefit: This removes a duplicated private construction and an inlined copy of it. The component subgroup is then the standard Mathlib object, so existing `AddSubgroup.ofClass` lemmas apply and readers do not have to check that a bespoke subgroup matches the library one.
